{{Quote|I was once a Jedi Knight, the same as your father.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
A '''Jedi Knight''' referred to a [[Jedi/Legends|member]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], who had completed their [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]] as a [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|student]] in the [[Jedi academy]], in addition to one-on-one training as a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] and the completion of the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]].

As a Knight and a full member of the Order, these individuals received assignments from the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Councils]] and strove to find peace, and maintain order within the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Making up the majority of the Order's members, the public was familiar with this title more than any other, and, thus, many addressed any Jedi as "Knight".<ref name="TJP" />

==Overview and history==
[[File:FNU.jpg|thumb|left|235px|Jedi Knights of the Old Republic: [[Cay Qel-Droma]], [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]], [[Nomi Sunrider]], and [[Tott Doneeta]].]]
{{Quote|For a hundred generations the Jedi have fought to protect the Republic!|Unidentified humanoid Jedi, [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]].|<ref name="Fall of Sith">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref>}}
[[25,783 BBY|Seven hundred and thirty]] years after the Order's founding on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] in the earliest days of galactic civilization, the Jedi Knights were brought into the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], working as peacekeepers for the fledgling government.<ref name="Timeline 15">[[Timeline 15: The Jedi Join the Republic]]</ref> A loose band of both philosophers and warriors, these early Knights had no central leadership, nor any formalized training at an academy; instead, they completed a series of tasks set by their master, who would then bestow upon them the rank of a Jedi Knight.<ref name="TJP" />

As the Order grew more centralized with the foundation of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], following the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], and the Republic's donation of the [[Sacred spire/Legends|Sacred spire]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] for use by the Knights, residing at the capital, the role of Knights in the Republic became more defined. Working as peacekeepers, diplomats, and investigators during peace time, the Knights helped to establish peace following the war. However, due to the High Council's seemingly complacent attitude during the [[Mandalorian Wars]], many Knights turned away from the Order and joined the [[Revan/Legends|Revanchist's]] [[Revanchist|movement]], which would eventually lead to the [[Jedi Civil War]].

When the Order recovered, the training of Padawans to Knighthood resumed more formally until the [[New Sith Wars]] and the creation of the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]] forced the Order to, once again, take on a militaristic way of life. When the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] was defeated, and the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] put into effect, formal training began again and the Order flourished.<ref name="TJP" />
[[File:LukeSkywalker-NEGTC.png|thumb|262x262px|Luke Skywalker, Jedi Knight]]
As the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] returned, and the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] swept across the Republic, all active Jedi Knights became [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi Generals]], and were required to lead the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] on the front lines against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. However, the Order was betrayed by the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]], whom they served, who was in reality the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. Sidious used his position as [[Supreme Commander (Republic)|Supreme Commander]] Palpatine to issue [[Contingency Orders for the Grand Army of the Republic: Order Initiation, Orders 1 Through 150|Executive]] [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], which demanded the slaughter of all Jedi and began the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|second major Jedi Purge]]. Loyal to the Republic, the troopers of the Grand Army cut down their generals without hesitation, while the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], under the command of a [[Dark side of the Force/Legends#Stage 3: Submission|fallen]] Jedi Knight, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|stormed]] the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant, and slaughtered the [[Jedi instructor|instructors]] and Initiates stationed there. While there were several Knights that survived the initial wave of what became known as the Great Jedi Purge, Vader, the newly-anoited [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], took personal charge of hunting down those Jedi who had escaped to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Eventually, during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Anakin Skywalker left the dark side, conquered Darth Vader from within and then saved his son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]], by destroying [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to [[Chosen One/Legends|bring balance to the Force]] in fulfilling an ancient Jedi prophecy.

After several decades of hiding at near extinction, the Order was [[New Jedi Order|reformed]] under Luke Skywalker, who, after the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] ended, established a new [[Jedi Praxeum]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] and began using the basic skills taught to him by the former [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]], [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], to train the next generation of Knights. For a time, Knighting was much less formal as it had been in the past during times of rebuilding, but eventually, Skywalker led the Order to flourish, and adapted many of the Old Order's customs on knighthood.<ref name="TJP" />

==Service to the Order==
[[File:Obi-Wan_Knighted_Episode_I_Canon.png|thumb|235px|Master Yoda bestows the rank of Jedi Knight upon Obi-Wan Kenobi.|left]]
{{Quote|Confer on you the level of Jedi Knight, the Council does.|Grand Master Yoda, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
Following the successful completion of a decade or more of one-on-one instruction from a master, Jedi Padawans were expected to pass the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]] and be [[Knighting Ceremony/Legends|raised]] to the rank of Knight. Only the High Council could promote a Padawan to the rank of Knight, though this rule was not always observed, especially in times when the Order was spread extremely thin or the Council could not be contacted for a great period of time. For those Jedi who did join this elite group of individuals, they were no longer attached to their master and were in charge of their own destiny. Knights were expected to continue their study in the Force, choosing between one of three fields of specialization so as to hone their personal strengths into the swords and shields of the Order. Either becoming a [[Jedi Guardian/Legends|Guardian]], [[Jedi Consular|Consular]], or [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Sentinel]], the Knights would accept solo missions from one of the four [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Councils]] that made best use of their skill sets.<ref name="TJP" />
[[File:KnightingCeremony-CW21.jpg|thumb|235px|Anakin Skywalker's Knighting Ceremony]]

On their own, Knights were responsible for maintaining the Order's public appearance as they traveled throughout the galaxy, floating along the currents of the Force as they sought to provide justice to suffering worlds. Taking on their own path of studying, Knights learned the third and final discipline of the Force known as [[Force power/Legends|Alter]]: which allowed the user to manipulate objects and others' minds with the application of the Force. Following the mastery of the Alter discipline and the completion of the study on specialized skills, a Knight might find themselves desiring to teach the next generation of Jedi. While not a mandatory practice, Knights could attend [[Jedi Temple Apprentice Tournament|tournaments]] at the Temple to see potential Padawans' exhibit their skills with the Force and a lightsaber. The Jedi of old warned against taking on an apprentice strictly out of duty, for this might ultimately lead to an irreconcilable incompatibility of Jedi and apprentice, leaving a Padawan without the proper guidance to gain a sufficient knowledge of the Force and Jedi Order skillsets in order to be successful during the Trials. Deeply focused meditation was performed before a selection was made, and while many Knights did choose to take on this sacred responsibility, there were a few that were unable to find a trainee who they felt would be the right fit or had no desire to take on such an all encompassing commitment.<ref name="TJP" />

Following successfully training a Padawan to knighthood, the High Council would consider raising the Knight to the rank of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]; though this was not always the case. Many Knights just simply were not promoted to Master if the Council did not feel that they had attained a knowledge of the Force that warranted the bestowment of such a title, or if the Force willed some other destiny for them. While some were promoted in old age, some Knights never ascended in rank. Because of the nature of the title and the importance of the Council, only Masters were elected to the Councils. On occasion a Knight would sit on the Council in the transition period between ascension in rank, though this was a simple technicality.<ref name="Ki-Adi DB">{{DB|character|kiadimundi|Ki-Adi-Mundi}}</ref> The most unusual case was that of Knight [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] appointment to the High Council by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. While the Council reluctantly accepted the appointment, they refused to raise Skywalker in ranks, maintaining their stance that he had not mastered his emotions entirely.<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:Leia_FOTJdppdf.jpg|thumb|250px|Knight [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].|left]]

When the Order was disbanded during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], no Knights were promoted as the majority of the Order had been slaughtered. It wasn't until [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] rebuilt the Order that the term Knight was reused. Due to the informality of the Order in its early years, many of the old traditions were not observed simply out of ignorance to their existence. Rudimentary Trials were established at the [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] [[Jedi Praxeum]] without knowledge of the Order's traditional tasks; these included demonstration of mastery of a set of skills and the ability to construct a lightsaber. Skywalker's inaugural class graduated in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] and were dispatched out into the galaxy to assist the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] in its endeavors to drive the Empire from civilized space.<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref> As more apprentices were taken, their masters would consult with Master Skywalker and could be granted permission to bestow the rank of knighthood following a successful mission that proved one's mettle; such was the case of [[Jaden Korr]] whose master, [[Kyle Katarn]], thought that his [[Mission to Vjun (Disciples of Ragnos crisis)|success]] on [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]] proved he had taught all Korr needed to know.<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

The first recorded public knighting ceremony was in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]] when Master Skywalker knighted [[Anakin Solo]], [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], [[Zekk]], [[Tenel Ka Djo|Tenel Ka]], [[Lusa]], [[Raynar Thul]], and [[Lowbacca]] for their year of service in aiding in the defeat of the [[Diversity Alliance]] and [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]]. Held at the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] in front of the entirety of the Order and representatives of the Republic, the ceremony consisted of a lightsaber salute and a ballad by Master [[Tionne Solusar]].<ref name="Young Jedi Knights: Crisis at Crystal Reef">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Crisis at Crystal Reef]]''</ref>

Several years later, following the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] and the procurement of several important [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]] and [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force|documents]], formal knighting ceremonies likened to that of the Old Order were reincorporated into the way of the Jedi. With the Coruscant [[New Jedi Temple|Temple]] rebuilt, ceremonies were once more held here in the [[Hall of Knighthood/Legends|Hall of Knighthood]].<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Jedi Knights were first mentioned in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]] and published in [[1976]]. The [[Hero of Tython|Jedi Knight]] is also a class in the Star Wars MMO, ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. This class is further customizable by selecting either the Sentinel or Guardian advanced classes.
The Jedi Knights commonly appear in fan films' plots, including in the famous [[w:c:swfans:Star Wars: Renaissance|''Star Wars: Renaissance'']], which introduces several fanon Knights.

Lucas himself has compared the Jedi Knights to various real world religious and spiritual orders, citing Christian or Buddhist monks and priests and the Knights Templar.<ref name="YouTube">{{YouTube|video=b0VJU1lmP3Y|text=Star Wars CV Jon Stewart Interview with George Lucas Pt 5|channel=channel/UCnJDCj7rCC0BEqylD4M9JJg|name=Daniel Geer}}</ref> [[The Making of Star Wars]] reveals that the Jedi were at one point named the Jedi Templar, indicating that specific order may have been an influence.

[[Wizards of the Coast]] ran a league for the [[Star Wars Trading Card Game]] called [[Jedi Nights]], a word play on Jedi Knights.<ref name="Wizards">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=swtcg/article/jedinights|text=Jedi Nights}}</ref>
